clue.text: Bank backs America in recession, without doubt

indicators.note: one piece backing another stands right behind it, so the word for bank comes after
something in recession is going backwards, so the letters for America are read from right to left

parts.note: to bank on someone is to depend on them, so bank gives a verb of trust

explanation.surface: A bank pulls its support from the American economy during a slump, and that is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns US into SU; 'backs' puts RELY behind it. Bank is the verb, as in bank on, not the money house.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of confidence: certainly, with no room for any question.

clue.text: Cartoonist depicted Al Capone, forgetting his initials

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so the gangster's initials are dropped from his nickname

parts.note: the Chicago gangster Al Capone was nicknamed Scarface
Al Capone's initials are A and C

explanation.surface: A newspaper cartoonist draws the gangster Al Capone but leaves off the initials in his caption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicted' is a link. Gerald Scarfe is a British political cartoonist famous for savage caricatures; 'forgetting' removes AC from SCARFACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Scarfe is a well-known British caricaturist, so he is an example of a cartoonist.

clue.text: Saying what one of scripture teacher's tasks is

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the British school subject covering scripture
correcting pupils' homework, marking, is one of a teacher's chores

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a religious studies teacher spends evenings doing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools RE (religious education) is the subject where scripture is taught, so an RE teacher's job includes RE marking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be remarking is to be commenting or observing out loud, so it is a synonym of saying.

clue.text: Spanish writer composed carol

indicators.note: composed suggests putting something together anew, so the letters of carol are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish author wrote a Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: Federico Garcia Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca, poet and dramatist of Blood Wedding, is a famous author from Spain.

clue.text: Something accidentally lost from small sack

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to sack a town is to plunder or pillage it

explanation.surface: Something has fallen out of a little bag by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' reads as a bag but is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillage is liquid or material that escapes by mistake, an accidental loss from a container.

clue.text: Writer Dylan Freud translated worthless novel

parts.note: a pen is something you write with, a writer in the crossword sense

indicators.note: translated suggests turning into another form, so the letters of Dylan Freud are rearranged

explanation.surface: A text by Dylan and Freud has been rendered into another language as a trashy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges DYLAN FREUD into NYDREADFUL. A penny dreadful was a cheap, lurid Victorian serial story sold for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny dreadfuls were cheap sensational Victorian fiction, the kind of pulp story with no literary value.

clue.text: Given assistance, fellow thanks worker

parts.note: Len is a man's name, standing for any fellow
ta is informal British for thanks
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A man thanks the labourer who helped him.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you; any man's name, here LEN, can stand for 'fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lent a hand is the idiom for having helped someone, so it matches given assistance.

clue.text: Community that settled in America, entering through Miami's harbour

indicators.note: the answer runs through the middle of the words Miami's harbour, entering at one end and leaving at the other

explanation.surface: Settlers arriving in America by sailing into the port at Miami.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Christian group of Swiss-German origin who settled in Pennsylvania and other American states.

clue.text: Making certain gunner is properly trained

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of gunner is are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Ensuring a soldier in the artillery has had the right training.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuring is guaranteeing that something happens, so it equals making certain.

clue.text: Fan, one into DReam, Kinks and Queen?

indicators.note: kinks are twists, so the letters of the band name are twisted out of shape around the I

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A fan of three bands: D:Ream, the Kinks and Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: D:Ream, the Kinks and Queen are all bands, so the surface is a music fan. 'Kinks' rearranges I and DREAM into ADMIRE; 'into' just places the I among the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiastic follower, someone who looks up to a performer.

clue.text: Check for building material used in supporting structure

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, so rein means check
taken as written
cement is a material used in building

explanation.surface: Inspect the materials going into a building's frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like inspect but is the verb restrain, as reins check a horse; 'used in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reinforcement is something added to strengthen and support, such as steel bars in concrete.

clue.text: Little orphan's attached to new nursemaids

indicators.note: one piece attached to another is joined right beside it, here following the letter for new

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical orphan, here with her possessive

explanation.surface: A small orphan has grown fond of the new nannies.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is an American comic-strip heroine, later the musical Annie.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannies are women employed to look after children, the same role as nursemaids.

clue.text: Convention supporting African country's tyrannical leaders

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: leaders are the front of the word, so the opening letters of tyrannical are taken

explanation.surface: A treaty that backs an African nation's despotic rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first two letters of 'tyrannical', TY; 'Convention' is the noun for accepted custom, not a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A formality is a customary procedure or rule of etiquette, which is what a convention is.

clue.text: A female winning McCartney's heart?

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of McCartney is taken

explanation.surface: A woman captures the affection of Paul McCartney.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress Jane Asher was Paul McCartney's girlfriend in the 1960s, so the whole clue describes her; 'heart' gives R, the middle of the nine-letter MCCARTNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Asher, the actress, was engaged to Paul McCartney in the 1960s, a woman who won his love.

clue.text: Motorway vehicles ultimately lining one behind the other? That can't be true

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of vehicles is taken

parts.note: vehicles lining up one behind the other are in a set pattern, like aircraft flying in a set arrangement

explanation.surface: Cars on a motorway queueing nose to tail, prompting someone to cry that it can't be right.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI. 'ultimately' takes the S ending 'vehicles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Misinformation is false or misleading content, something that is not true.

clue.text: I note something wrong: prophet sounding hypocritical

parts.note: N, for north, is one of the compass points that crosswords call notes
a sin is a wrongdoing

indicators.note: sounding means pronounced, so a word for prophet is replaced by letters that sound the same

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who sees the future

explanation.surface: Someone notes a misdeed and calls a prophet a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns SEER into CERE, the same sound spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere means not genuine in what one says, which is how a hypocrite behaves.

clue.text: Be privy to what cleric brought up during row

indicators.note: one piece happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: to row is to propel a boat with an oar, so row gives that paddle

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eh is the exclamation 'what?' when someone does not hear
Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric

explanation.surface: Learn what a clergyman raised during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses both short words as one run, giving VERHE to go inside the paddle. Row is the boating verb here, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To be privy to something is to share secret knowledge of it, as you do when catching words not meant for you.

clue.text: Cook gave a diner this nut roast, maybe

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters of gave a diner this are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef served a restaurant customer a meatless nut roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef but is the anagram signal; 'maybe' marks nut roast as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut roast is a classic meat-free main course, an example of food for those who avoid meat.

clue.text: Top breed of cow

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a knitted pullover
the Channel Island cattle breed known for rich creamy milk

explanation.definitionFit: A jumper-style knitted garment for the upper body, and also a dairy cattle breed from the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Insecure businessman engages a detective

indicators.note: to engage is to hold or take in, so the words Insecure businessman hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A nervous executive hires a private investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engages' reads as hires but signals that the words hold the answer. Inspector Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector John Rebus is the detective hero of Ian Rankin's crime novels.

clue.text: It's said worker needs twenty-four hours for bathroom installation

indicators.note: it's said means spoken out loud, so the words for worker and a day are heard together

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the classic crossword worker, and twenty-four hours make a day; 'needs' joins the two

explanation.surface: A labourer needs a whole day to fit something in a bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the insect and the day give the French-derived word for a low washing basin; 'needs' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin for washing, a fixture fitted in a bathroom.

clue.text: Flowing waste causing disease within eastern border?

indicators.note: within means inside, so the word for disease goes into the word for border

parts.note: a fence marks the border of a property
flu is a common disease

explanation.surface: Sewage spreading illness across a frontier in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link, and 'within' sets the illness just after the first letter of the border word. Border reads as a frontier in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluence is matter that flows out, such as sewage or outflow from a factory.

clue.text: Relative wanting smutty article censored

indicators.note: censored means cut, so the article is cut out of the word for smutty

parts.note: smutty means dirty, unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family member wants a dirty piece of writing banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link, and 'article' is grammar, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, the brother of a parent, so he is a relative.

clue.text: Play match beginning with goal

indicators.note: the word for match begins with the word for goal, which stands in front

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
a game is a match

explanation.surface: A football match opens with an early goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is the theatre noun: Endgame is a play by Samuel Beckett.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's Endgame is a famous play, so the title is an example of one.

clue.text: Servants need energy, you say, at the start

parts.note: to lack something is to need it
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letters of the words you and say

explanation.surface: Someone claims staff should get going early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes Y and S from 'you say'; it is not a homophone here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackeys are servants, originally liveried footmen, now also servile followers.

clue.text: Once more negotiates tactical withdrawals

definitions.meaning: to treat is to negotiate, so to do it again is to treat again
armies pulling back on purpose to a safer position

explanation.definitionFit: Treating means negotiating, so doing it again fits the first sense; military pullbacks fit the second.

clue.text: Sherry is in short supply, my boy

indicators.note: something in short supply is cut short, so the last letter of the word for sherry is dropped

parts.note: Jerez is the Spanish town that gave sherry its name, and the Spanish name for the wine

explanation.surface: Someone complains that sherry is running low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. Sherry takes its name from Jerez in Andalusia; shortened it loses its Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy is a boy's name, and crosswords use boy for any male first name.
